item.title: Chinese Defense Minister visits Italy
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
BEIJING, Nov. 17 -- Chinese Defense Minister Admiral Dong Jun visited Italy upon the invitation of Italian Defense Minister Guido Crosetto on November 16, 2026. The two sides held an in-depth exchange of views on bilateral relations and military-to-military ties, the international and regional situation, and issues of common interest. They agreed to further promote military-to-military relations and jointly safeguard regional and global peace and stability. Prior to the talks, Minister Crosetto hosted a welcome ceremony for Minister Dong.

item.title: China Coast Guard ship Sandu concludes visit to Malaysia
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
BEIJING, Nov. 16--The China Coast Guard (CCG) ship Sandu (Hull 5308) concluded its four-day friendly visit to Penang, Malaysia, on November 13, and set sail for home. During the transit, vessels from China and Malaysia conducted maritime formation training and a communications exercise. In the formation training, the CCG ship Sandu and the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) ship KM Tun Fatimah (Hull 8305) shifted between column and line-abreast formations. During the visit, the Chinese and Malaysian sides held high-level meetings and conducted multiple training subjects, including a maritime search and rescue tabletop exercise, formation training, and a communications exercise. The two sides also hosted activities such as open-ship days, cultural and sports exchanges, and a deck receptionevent. (Video Editor: Yang Xueqing)

item.title: Xi urges breaking new ground in high-quality development of Greater Bay Area
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, visits an artificial island of the Shenzhen-Zhongshan Link, a sea-crossing project connecting the cities of Shenzhen, Zhongshan and Guangzhou, in south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 16, 2026. Xi made an inspection tour on Monday in Zhongshan, south China's Guangdong Province. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi) ZHONGSHAN, Guangdong, Nov. 16 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Monday urged efforts to thoroughly study and implement the guiding principles of the fifth plenary session of the 20th Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, and to strive to break new ground in the high-quality development of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area. Xi, also general secretary of the CPC Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks during an inspection tour in Zhongshan, south China's Guangdong Province. Stressing fully and faithfully implementing the decisions and arrangements made at the plenary session and leveraging new progress in persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance, Xi urged a better job in advancing integrated development along the Pearl River Estuary. Visiting an artificial island of the Shenzhen-Zhongshan Link, a sea-crossing project connecting the cities of Shenzhen, Zhongshan and Guangzhou, Xi demanded efforts to further enhance the management and operation of this mega transport project to better serve the development of the Greater Bay Area. At an industrial park in Zhongshan, Xi learned about local efforts to absorb industrial transfers, transform and upgrade traditional industries, and develop emerging industries. Building the Greater Bay Area is a major strategic plan made by the CPC Central Committee, Xi said, calling on cities along the Pearl River Estuary including Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Zhuhai, Dongguan and Zhongshan to play a pioneering role. Xi expressed the hope that Zhongshan would seize the opportunities, take reform and innovation as the fundamental driving force, improve regional cooperation mechanisms, foster a sound business environment, and vigorously promote the deep integration of technological innovation and industrial innovation. Speaking to representatives of small and medium-sized enterprises and sci-tech personnel, Xi encouraged them to make greater contributions to the development of Guangdong and the Greater Bay Area and China's greater self-reliance and strength in science and technology. Xi also visited the Museum of Dr. Sun Yat-sen and laid a floral basket before his bronze statue. This year marks the 160th anniversary of Sun's birth. On the new journey, it is necessary to emulate, inherit and promote his invaluable spirit, and inspire all Chinese people at home and abroad to unite and strive to build a great country and advance national rejuvenation through Chinese modernization, Xi said. During the inspection tour, Xi also stressed the need to continuously steer the economy toward innovation-driven and high-quality development, ensure that major targets and tasks for the year are fulfilled, and get the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) off to a good start. item.title: Shenzhen summit marks first face-to-face meeting among Chinese, Russian, U.S. heads of state in history
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
BEIJING, Nov. 16 (Xinhua) -- The meeting of the Chinese, Russian and U.S. heads of state in south China's Shenzhen will be the first face-to-face meeting in history involving the top leaders of the three countries, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said on Monday. Chinese President Xi Jinping will hold a China-Russia-U.S. summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump in Shenzhen on Nov. 19, according to the ministry. Mao said the heads of state will have an in-depth exchange of views on maintaining world peace and promoting strategic stability in major country relations, which is of groundbreaking significance. Noting that China, Russia and the United States are all founding members of the UN and permanent members of the UN Security Council, Mao said the three countries have fought together to achieve the victory of the World Anti-Fascist War. Under current circumstances, the three countries shoulder the important responsibility of cooperating to address global challenges and promote world peace and stability, said Mao. Strengthening communication, managing and controlling differences, and stabilizing relations among China, Russia and the United States serve the interests of the three countries, meet the expectations of the international community, and are conducive to stabilizing the world situation and promoting dialogue and cooperation, she said.

item.title: The Philippines Should Rein in Dangerous Words and Actions of Certain Politicians: Defense Spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
BEIJING, Nov. 13-- "Driven by political prejudice and self-interest, certain Filipino politicians made remarks which run counter to the solemn commitment the Philippine government has made to China on the Taiwan question. We strongly deplore and firmly oppose such statements," said Senior Colonel Chen Xi, spokesperson for China's defense ministry, at a press briefing on Friday. According to reports, the Philippine Defense Secretary said in a recent interview that with 200,000 Filipinos residing in Taiwan, the Philippines is preparing for all contingencies, and that it would be counterproductive for China to try to seize Taiwan by force. In response to that, thespokesperson noted that the Taiwan question is purely China's internal affair. How to resolve it is a matter for the Chinese people, which brooks no foreign interference. The spokesperson also emphasized that China is firm in its resolve to safeguard sovereignty and territorial integrity and achieve national reunification. "We urges the Philippine side to rein in the dangerous words and actions of these politicians, abide by the one-China principle, and take real actions to maintain stable China-Philippines relations," stressed the spokesperson.
